directives.meaning: Look into the issue in detail: its causes, effects and implications.

sentences.text: Of the many Sufi silsilas, the Chishti and Suhrawardi orders gained the widest following in north India during the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries.
Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti established the Chishti order in India and settled at Ajmer.
His spiritual line passed through Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki to Baba Fariduddin Ganj-i-Shakar, some of whose verses appear in the Adi Granth.
Nizamuddin Auliya and Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Delhi were the most celebrated Chishti saints, mingling with common people and conversing in Hindawi.
Chishti saints popularised sama, musical recitation often set to Hindi verses, to evoke nearness to God.
The Chishtis kept aloof from state politics and shunned the company of rulers and nobles.
The Suhrawardi order, which entered India at about the same time as the Chishtis, was confined largely to Bengal and the Deccan.
Unlike the Chishtis, Suhrawardi saints did not embrace poverty and accepted state service, some holding posts in the ecclesiastical department.
Both orders fostered a climate of tolerance, and their message of harmony remains relevant to India's pluralism.
